target_name: Contributed-capital dependence confirmed by fresh dilution
rationale: The construct is largely a stock-variable restatement of the archive's gen-0 "issuance by accumulated-deficit firms" and gen-1 "chronic equity funding" signals — (ceq−re)/at is the mechanical complement of retained-earnings intensity already tested — and its negative-return prediction from high contributed capital plus fresh issuance is close to a repackaging of the published net/composite share-issuance anomaly and the Ball et al. contributed-vs-retained-earnings decomposition.

This is a cosmetic recombination of two already-tested archive signals — "Payout escalation outrunning cash-flow improvement" (same structure, fmb 0.10, alpha 0.004) and "Payout maintained through revenue contraction" (same sale-growth leg) — and GROWTH(dvc) on a small or zero base will produce an unstable, heavily-truncated left leg rather than a cleaner mechanism test.

target_name: Peer-abnormal dilution with peer-abnormal revenue weakness
rationale: Applying industry demeaning to the archive's best-Sharpe csho-versus-sale pair is incremental rather than conceptually new, but it poses a well-defined and unresolved question (firm-specific versus sector-cycle) on a pair that already showed jointly-signed cross-sectional and portfolio evidence, so it is worth one test.

target_name: Dividend retrenchment under weak obligation coverage
rationale: The expression is internally consistent with its stated positive sign, but the hypothesis runs directly against the well-documented negative post-announcement drift following dividend cuts and omissions (Michaely-Thaler-Womack), and as a near-mirror of eight already-tested payout-rigidity signals it risks being read as a sign flip rather than a new mechanism.

The denominator (che + oancf) can cross zero, so the most cash-burning firms produce large *negative* ratios that sort into the "safe" leg while marginally-positive denominators explode upward — the signal is non-monotone in the very distress it claims to measure, and 1% winsorization does not repair a sign discontinuity.

target_name: Frequency of paying dividends while losing money
rationale: The joint-episode count is a genuine sharpening of the archive's additive pay-plus-loss composite, but the low end pools non-payers with healthy payers at a count of zero, and this is the ninth instance of the SUB(RANK(payout-ish), RANK(che/lct)) template whose recurring pattern of significant negative alpha alongside insignificant FMB slopes strongly suggests the liquidity leg, not the payout leg, is generating the spread.
